propositions: Gate operations (transition closed, review-plan, verify-completion) emit no incremental output to stdout/stderr between invocation and final verdict, causing supervisor stall watchdogs with default 600s budgets to kill healthy long-running calls

The two longest phases of gate operations (27s material-assembly prologue and 40s overlap-corpus retrieval) contain no instrumentation at any log level, and local compute phases log only after completion, not during execution
An autonomous agent orchestrating rebar was killed mid-epic-close by its harness's stream watchdog after 600s silence, leaving the epic and story stranded in-progress despite all code changes landed

ADR 0089 defers progress-emission behind async runner migration and intentionally permits time-to-first-token silence, but does not block a periodic daemon-thread liveness heartbeat compatible with blocking sync code

Existing test suite (test_llm_timeouts.py) pins silence-tolerance and absence of total-runtime timers as correct behaviour, constraining any remediation to purely additive emission that does not truncate healthy long runs
